faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, the national minimum wage of $26.44 per hour gives $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44 per year. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading rate in Australia?
faqs.a: Casual employees covered by the national minimum wage or most awards receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For the national minimum wage, that means $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. The loading is paid instead of entitlements like paid leave. Always check your award or agreement for the exact rate.

faqs.q: What is the NRL salary cap for 2026?
faqs.a: For the 2026 season, the NRL’s top-30 salary cap is $11.55 million base, plus a $100,000 motor vehicle allowance and a $300,000 veteran and developed player allowance, totalling $11.95 million per club. This is a team-wide cap, not an individual player limit. Players can also earn unlimited amounts from non-club sponsors and certain benefits like education fees outside the cap.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly Pay to Annual, Fortnightly, and Weekly Figures

If you know your hourly rate, you can estimate your annual gross pay using a simple formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For most full-time employees under awards or the national system, the standard week is 38 ordinary hours. Our [the timesheet](/) uses this assumption unless you enter a different number.

For example, the **national minimum wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. That gives:

- Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.90
- Fortnightly: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80
- Annual: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44

These figures come from the Fair Work Commission’s National Minimum Wage Order 2026. The same calculation works for any hourly rate, but remember it assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

## The National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The national minimum wage is the legal floor for award/agreement-free employees. Many workers are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or role. You can find the correct rate for your job using our [pay guides](/blog) or the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for not getting paid leave. For the national minimum wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. If you are casual, use our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page to see how it affects your pay. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the checkbox on the timesheet adds it for you.

## Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of **12%** (from 2026–27) on your ordinary earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is paid **on top** of your gross pay, not deducted from it. So your total employment cost is your gross pay plus 12% super. For more details, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies marginal tax rates for 2026–27:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool to estimate what you keep after tax and Medicare.

## Average Earnings in Australia

The Australian Bureau of Statistics’ Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 show:

- Full-time adult ordinary time: $2,083.70 per week ($108,352.40 annual)
- All employees total earnings (including part-time): $1,579.20 per week ($82,118.40 annual)

These averages help you see where your hourly rate sits compared to the broader workforce. Our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page has more comparisons.

## What Is the NRL Salary Cap?

For a very different perspective on annual pay, consider professional rugby league. **What is the NRL salary cap?** It is the total amount each NRL club can spend on its top 30 players in a season. For 2026, the base cap is $11.55 million, plus a $100,000 motor vehicle allowance and a $300,000 veteran and developed player allowance, making a total of $11.95 million per club. This is a team cap, not an individual limit. Individual players can earn additional income from non-club sponsors, representative payments, and certain benefits outside the cap. While NRL players are not paid by the hour, their annual contracts can be converted to an equivalent hourly rate for comparison – but the cap shows how high-end sports salaries are structured very differently from award wages. For more on how job pay varies across industries, see [job pay](/topics/job-pay).

## Important Notes on Our Calculations

All annual figures on this site are estimates based on the formula hourly rate × hours per week × 52. They assume:

- The same rate every week
- No unpaid overtime
- No penalty rates or allowances
- No salary sacrifice

Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this reference. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. For precise rates, always check the Fair Work Ombudsman, Fair Work Commission, and the Australian Taxation Office.

Use our [reference tables](/data) to look up minimum wages, award classifications, and historical rates. And if you need to calculate your own pay, start with [the timesheet](/).
